title: Aeneas and the founding of Rome (Virgil)
subtitle: The Aeneid
subject: mythologie
description: In the Aeneid, Virgil tells how Aeneas, a prince who escaped from Troy, crosses the Mediterranean to found the bloodline of Rome.

hero.hook: A Trojan on the run carries his father on his shoulders: Rome is born from that exile.

blocks.text: The **Aeneid** is the great poem of **Virgil**. It tells the long journey of **Aeneas**, a Trojan prince who survived the fall of Troy. Guided by the gods, he crosses the Mediterranean to found, in Italy, the line that will lead to Rome.
It is not only an adventure story. It is the founding myth of Roman power, written to give Rome a past as glorious as Homer's.

At the end of the 1st century BC, after years of civil war, the emperor **Augustus** wants to secure his power. He commissions Virgil to write an epic worthy of Homer. The work also serves [[Augustan propaganda]]: it links the ruler to a divine hero.

blocks.caption: Virgil, poet of the Aeneid, singer of a Rome willed by destiny

blocks.text: Virgil works on it for eleven years (29-19 BC). The first six books follow the wandering at sea. The next six tell the war in Italy. He writes in [[dactylic hexameters]], the verse of the great ancient epics.
Virgil dies in **19** BC and asks for the manuscript to be burned, judging it unfinished. Augustus forbids anyone to obey. Rome's national epic appears against its author's will.

sections.title: Flight from Troy and love in Carthage

blocks.text: As Troy burns, at the end of the [[Trojan War]], Aeneas, son of the goddess **Venus** and the mortal Anchises, is ordered to flee. He leaves carrying his father on his shoulders and his son Ascanius by the hand, and takes the [[Penates]], the gods of the household. That gesture defines [[Roman pietas]]: duty to family, to the gods and to destiny.

blocks.caption: Aeneas flees burning Troy, father and son with him

blocks.text: In Carthage, he falls in love with Queen **Dido**. But [[Jupiter]], king of the Roman gods, calls him back to his mission. Aeneas sails away. Dido kills herself and curses his descendants: the myth explains the future hatred between Rome and Carthage, long before the [[Punic Wars]].
Aeneas' son Ascanius is also called Iulus. The [[Julii]] family, which included Julius Caesar and Augustus, claimed this divine descent through Venus.

After a journey down into the underworld, Aeneas lands in **Latium**, in central Italy. King **Latinus** promises him his daughter **Lavinia**. But prince **Turnus**, backed by [[Juno]], a goddess hostile to the Trojans, starts a war.
Aeneas defeats Turnus and founds **Lavinium**. Later his son founds [[Alba Longa]], where Romulus and Remus will be born. The myth ties Troy to Rome in a single chain.

events.title: The flight of Aeneas
events.detail: He saves his father, his son and the household gods.

events.title: Dido
events.detail: A broken love, a curse on Rome.

events.title: Victory over Turnus
events.detail: Lavinium is founded, the first step toward Rome.

blocks.text: In the Middle Ages, Virgil becomes an almost prophetic sage. Dante makes him his guide in [[The Divine Comedy]]. But Aeneas is not a cheerful hero: he carries the weight of destiny. Rome is born from an exile, a sacrificed love and a war.
In the **Aeneid**, Virgil makes **Aeneas**, the survivor of Troy, the mythical ancestor of Rome. The hero embodies **pietas**: duty before desire, destiny before personal happiness.
